title: CBDT Notifies Foreign Assets Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026 for Small Taxpayers
content:
# CBDT Notifies Foreign Assets Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026 for Small Taxpayers

Ek important update hai. Government ne "Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers–Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026" (FAST-DS) notify kiya hai. This is a one-time voluntary disclosure scheme, bringing much-needed clarity for small taxpayers with undisclosed foreign assets or income.

**Key Highlights:**

*   **Scheme Name:** Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers–Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), 2026.
*   **Notification Details:** The Central Government notified these Rules through G.S.R. 732(E), dated August 14, 2026, vide Notification No. 114/2026/F. No. 370142/18/2026-TPL.
*   **Effective Date:** The Rules have come into force from August 16, 2026.
*   **Purpose:** This scheme offers a one-time window for eligible taxpayers to regularise specified undisclosed foreign assets, undisclosed foreign income, or foreign assets that, though acquired from explained/taxed sources, were not disclosed in relevant schedules of the income-tax return. It also provides immunity from further tax, penalty, and prosecution under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015 for the disclosed items.
*   **Eligibility:** The scheme is primarily for small taxpayers like students, young professionals, and relocated non-resident Indians. Eligibility also extends to an assessee who was a resident in India in the relevant previous year.
*   **Categories of Disclosure:**
    *   **Category 1:** Undisclosed foreign assets or income not previously offered to tax. The aggregate value should not exceed ₹1 crore. The effective tax rate is 60%.
    *   **Category 2:** Foreign assets acquired from explained/taxed sources or during non-residency but not disclosed in ITR. The aggregate value should not exceed ₹5 crore. A flat fee of ₹1 lakh is payable.
*   **Valuation Date:** The fair market value of assets proposed to be declared will be determined as of March 31, 2026.
*   **Last Date for Declaration:** Taxpayers can file declarations until December 31, 2026. No declaration can be filed after this date.
*   **Process:** The entire declaration process is envisaged to be undertaken electronically in Form 1. Detailed FAQs have also been issued by CBDT to explain the scheme.
